ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Most bettors lose money before they ever place a bad pick.
The reason is bankroll math.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common assumption: bet whatever feels right on games you like. $50 here, $200 there, $20 on a parlay.
That's not a strategy. That's noise.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Flat betting a fixed unit, typically 1 to 2% of your total bankroll per play, is the single most effective way to survive variance.
At 54% accuracy, wild bet sizing will still blow you up.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: $1,000 bankroll. Your unit is $15 (1.5%).
A 10-game losing streak costs you $150. You're still in the game.
Same streak betting $100 per game? You're down 15% and tilting.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
The edge compounds slowly. Protecting the bankroll is what lets it compound at all.
Smaller units, longer runway, better decisions under pressure.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Bankroll math isn't glamorous. It's what separates bettors who last from ones who reload and disappear. The unit size matters more than the pick.
